results.reason: The memo identifies the automatic five-year renewal, the 270/240-day notice requirement and the lock-in risk. However, it misstates the window as about June 3 – June 23, 2026, a 20-day window. It never explains that this is effectively a 30-day window; 240 days before expiry is about July 3, 2026.

Issue 2 identifies the all glass and PET, any beverage, worldwide exclusivity. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass, beer only, U.S./Canada scope and treats Harrowgate as bound by the executed text.
Issue 6 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 and expiry of the objection period on September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issues 3–4 explain that the amended § 11.2 drops recall costs from the exclusions and limits the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims under § 9.1(c). They note recall and product-liability exposure is now subject to the six-month fee cap.

Issue 5 identifies new § 14.4, which allows assignment without consent to Affiliates or successors. It does not mention assignment to a competitor, and it does not note that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, which makes the restriction one-sided.
Issue 10 states that § 15.2 ranks written amendments first, then the Supply Agreement, and that the Amendment qualifies as a written amendment. This means the Amendment controls.
The memo states the § 11.1 cap is the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to the Partner and lists issues item by item. Each item has a 'Where' location and a 'Recommended fix'.
The memo proposes specific language, including a restored § 11.2, a narrowed § 3.1, a revised § 2.2 renewal clause and a revised § 14.4.
The memo treats the objection window as closed and the increase as binding.
The memo treats the executed § 3.1 as governing and recommends renegotiation. It does not claim the term sheet binds the parties.
